answer.note: The four ref files are identical boilerplate and give no file-specific priority, so I chose from the code. The target is dogwhistle/visibility.py (C). It is the only candidate with ARMS = ("codeword","public","explicit"). Its receive() (lines 141-187) resumes from receiver_progress.json and raises on a trial-order mismatch. It writes ledger.json with private=True, then writes the public digest of the ledger bytes. dogwhistle/study.py (A) supplies the helpers it imports: checkpoint, write(private=), digest, invoke and ensure_published. Those helpers decide whether the checkpoint and private-ledger behaviour is real. dogwhistle/honest.py (D) has a near-identical receive() but only two arms, so it is a decoy. dogwhistle/heldout.py (B) has a sender-seal-bound receiver with 180 trials, not three arms. Suggested 60-minute split: C 35 min, A 15, D 6, B 4. I did not run any code.

input.note: The four ref files are identical boilerplate and give no file-specific priority, so I chose from the code. The target is dogwhistle/visibility.py (C). It is the only candidate with ARMS = ("codeword","public","explicit"). Its receive() (lines 141-187) resumes from receiver_progress.json and raises on a trial-order mismatch. It writes ledger.json with private=True, then writes the public digest of the ledger bytes. dogwhistle/study.py (A) supplies the helpers it imports: checkpoint, write(private=), digest, invoke and ensure_published. Those helpers decide whether the checkpoint and private-ledger behaviour is real. dogwhistle/honest.py (D) has a near-identical receive() but only two arms, so it is a decoy. dogwhistle/heldout.py (B) has a sender-seal-bound receiver with 180 trials, not three arms. Suggested 60-minute split: C 35 min, A 15, D 6, B 4. I did not run any code.
